precedence_rules.note: ADOPTED in references/10-conflict-resolution.md (P2b). Rule ids R1..R6 form a precedence ladder applied in ascending order, first match wins; R7 DEFAULT-FILL is not a conflict rule and is forbidden in rules_invoked by G-14. rules_invoked is listed in ascending ladder order and mirrors rule_names_as_proposed positionally.
precedence_rules.evaluation_order: strict ladder, lowest id first; the first rule that discriminates between the competing sources wins

rules.name: CODE-SUPREMACY
rules.statement: A statutory, regulatory or code requirement outranks every user statement, including an explicit one.

rules.name: SPECIFICITY
rules.statement: Among competing user statements of the same class, the one that is more specific wins: a value tied to a named level, element or condition beats a bare global value.

rules.name: QUANTITY-OVER-SUMMARY
rules.statement: A stated total loses to the stated parts that produce it. Parts are measurements; totals are usually summaries.

rules.name: BUILDABILITY
rules.statement: A value that cannot be built - negative dimension, head above floor-to-floor, negative clearance, element outside its host - loses to any value that can be built.

rules.name: MODULE-ALIGNMENT
rules.statement: A value that preserves the stated dimensional module or grid outranks one that breaks it.

rules.name: LATER-STATEMENT
rules.statement: Same class, same specificity, and no rule above discriminates: the statement appearing later in the source wins.

non_conflict_fallback.name: DEFAULT-FILL
non_conflict_fallback.statement: A documented default from references/09-defaults.md may fill a silence but may never decide a conflict. A default that appears in a conflicts entry is a bug.
